Who contributed what, under which abbreviation. The abbreviations appear in
every data filename in both archives, so this table is needed to read them.

## Spada et al. (2011)

From table 1 of the paper.

| Abbreviation | Code | Author or user | Method |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Bl | ABAQUS | B. Lund | Finite elements, flat-Earth approximation |
| Gs | TABOO | G. Spada | Viscoelastic normal modes |
| Gs | PMTF | G. Spada | Polar motion transfer function, viscoelastic normal modes |
| Gsa | ALMA | G. Spada | Post-Widder inversion |
| Pg | ABAQUS | P. Gasperini | Finite elements |
| Rr | FastLove-HiDeg | R. E. M. Riva | Viscoelastic normal modes |
| Vb | MHPLove | V. R. Barletta | High-precision Love numbers in Mathematica |
| Vk | VILMA | V. Klemann | Spectral finite elements |

Which contributor covered which test is recorded in each case file under
`reference_data.contributors`, and is shown on the
[cases page](../results/index.qmd).

::: {.callout-note}
## Two abbreviations that are easy to confuse

`MS` is the SELEN and TABOO results of Melini and Spada. In the benchmark A
plotting script the same series is labelled `MS` in the legend while its file
is named `A-fig10-TABOO_256.dat`, because benchmark A was computed with TABOO
and the other four cases with SELEN.

`SK` is Kachuck's giapy and `KS` is Simon and James's PGCcalc. They differ by
the order of two letters and appear in adjacent columns of every figure.
:::

The VEGA solution of ZM is the reference for all five cases. Table 6 of the
paper records the coverage: every code contributed case A, all but WWa
contributed case B, and five contributed each of C, D and E.
